title: H⁰-integral of a function vanishing off a measurable set that meets the domain in at most one point
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and H⁰ = μHE[0], the normalized 0-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P. Let C ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set (not assumed measurable), K ⊆ ℝ^P a measurable set, x ∈ ℝ^P, and F : ℝ^P → ℝ with F(z) = 0 for every z ∉ K. If C ∩ K ⊆ {x}, then ∫_C F dH⁰ = 1_C(x)·F(x); that is, the Bochner integral of F with respect to the restricted measure H⁰⌞C (μHE[0].restrict C) equals (Set.indicator C F)(x), which is F(x) if x ∈ C and 0 otherwise.
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C K : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (F : Euclid P → ℝ), MeasurableSet K → (∀ z, z ∉ K → F z = 0) → C ∩ K ⊆ {x} → ∫ z in C, F z ∂μHE[0] = C.indicator F x
